objective: Demonstrate AVR ATmega32 delay programs routine 5.
theory: AVR is an 8-bit RISC architecture by Microchip/Atmel featuring 32 general-purpose 8-bit registers (R0-R31) and single-cycle execution for most instructions.
algorithm: 1. Load byte from SRAM address 0x0100 into register R16.
2. Load immediate value 5 into register R17.
4. Store result from R16 to SRAM address 0x0101.
flowchart: START -> Execute Delay Programs Step 1 -> Process Data -> Verify Flags/Result -> END
assembly_code:
; AVR ATmega32 - Delay Programs Ex 5
lds r16, 0x0100
ldi r17, 5
add r16, r17
sts 0x0101, r16
step_by_step_execution: Step 1: Fetch and decode Delay Programs instruction for AVR (ATmega32/328P).
Step 2: Read input operands from memory / registers.
Step 3: Execute ALU operation for Delay Programs.
Step 4: Update status flags (Z, CY, S, P).
Step 5: Store final result into memory.
explanation: This program demonstrates delay programs on the AVR (ATmega32/328P) architecture.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to clear carry or flags before loop.

viva_questions.q: How many general-purpose working registers are in AVR?
What is the execution clock speed of AVR?
viva_questions.a: Most instructions execute in 1 clock cycle (1 MIPS per MHz).

practical_applications: Used in embedded control systems for delay programs.
Commonly used in real-time sensor processing on AVR (ATmega32/328P).
